title: Presentation and compactification independence of the tensor transpose
statement:
Fix primes $p
e\ell$, $q=p^a$ with $a\ge1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X	o Y$ a smooth separated finite-type $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small pro-etale sites, the derived pullback and tensor, and the constructible exceptional functor $Rf^!$ [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Put $\omega_f=Rf^!A_Y$.
Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, put $M=Lf^*K$, and let $	heta_{f,K}:M\otimes_A^L\omega_f	o Rf^!K$ denote the projection-and-counit transpose specified in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. For two compactifications $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,r:\overline X	o Y)$ and $c'=(j':X\hookrightarrow\overline X',r':\overline X'	o Y)$, write $F_c=Rr_*j_!$, $G_c=
u_X^* f_c^	imes R
u_{Y,*}$, and $\omega_c=G_cA_Y$. Here $
u$ is the etale/pro-etale site comparison, and $f_c^	imes$ is the ordinary-etale right adjoint to compact support. Use the canonical comparisons and the bounded etale-origin Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], with the finite-type compactifications (hence finite-dimensional proper parts) of [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For any chosen etale-origin witnesses realizing $M\otimes^L\omega_c$ and $M\otimes^L\omega_{c'}$, let $	heta^c_K$ and $	heta^{c'}_K$ be the respective transposes of symmetry, inverse projection, the counit at $A_Y$, and the unitor. If $b:G_c\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{c'}$ is the canonical comparison of right adjoints, then
$$b_K\circ	heta^c_K=	heta^{c'}_K\circ(1_M\otimes b_{A_Y}).$$
For fixed compactification, changing either etale-origin witness leaves this transpose unchanged under its canonical identification. The identifications of these maps are the identity for identical choices and satisfy the cocycle identity for three choices. They identify each realization with the specified $	heta_{f,K}$; no adjunction on arbitrary unbounded pro-etale objects is asserted.

proof.text: Use $F_c$ for pro-etale compact support and write $\Phi_c^{H,L}:\operatorname{Hom}(F_cH,L)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H,G_cL)$ for the comparison-class bijection. All its applications below lie in its domain: [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] puts $M=Lf^*K$ in $D^b_{ctf}$; [thm-sf-preservation-class] puts $\omega_c=G_cA_Y$ and $G_cK$ in $D^b_c$ (transport the bounds along the canonical comparison with the constructible exceptional functor). Thus [lem-sf-tensor-ctf] puts $H_c=M\otimes^L\omega_c$ in $D^b_c$. Both $H_c$ and $\omega_c$ have bounded etale origins by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. The same holds at $c'$. The proper compactification spaces have finite dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Hence [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] applies to these sources and to $L=A_Y,K$, with no unrestricted pro-etale adjunction.

source.place: Domain check for the canonical tensor formula

proof.text:
Put $\rho:F_c\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{c'}$ and $b:G_c\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{c'}$. Compatibility of the Hom bijections in [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] reads
$$\Phi_{c'}^{H,L}(a\rho_H^{-1})=b_L\Phi_c^{H,L}(a).$$
Define $\varepsilon_{c,L}=(\Phi_c^{G_cL,L})^{-1}(1_{G_cL})$ for the bounded constructible $L$ used here. Naturality in the source gives $(\Phi_c^{H,L})^{-1}(v)=\varepsilon_{c,L}F_c(v)$. Apply the displayed compatibility at $H=G_cA_Y$, $L=A_Y$, $a=\varepsilon_{c,A_Y}$ and use this inverse formula at $c'$: one obtains
$$\varepsilon_{c',A_Y}F_{c'}(b_{A_Y})\rho_{\omega_c}=\varepsilon_{c,A_Y}.$$
These are the counits on the comparison class, obtained from its stated natural bijections.

source.place: Counit compatibility extracted from the natural comparison-class Hom bijections

proof.text:
Write $P_c(N,K)=\operatorname{PF}^c_{f,N,K}$. For $N=\omega_c,\omega_{c'}$ these maps are invertible and natural in $N$ by [fix-prop-projection-formula]. The compactification square is precisely [lem-fix-projection-compactification-comparison]:
$$\rho_{\omega_c\otimes M}P_c(\omega_c,K)=P_{c'}(\omega_c,K)(\rho_{\omega_c}\otimes1_K).$$
Compose its two sides with inverse projections, and then use projection naturality for $b_A:\omega_c\to\omega_{c'}$ (here $A$ abbreviates $A_Y$). With $q=F_{c'}(b_A)\rho_{\omega_c}$ this gives
$$P_{c'}(\omega_{c'},K)^{-1}F_{c'}(b_A\otimes1_M)\rho_{\omega_c\otimes M}=(q\otimes1_K)P_c(\omega_c,K)^{-1}.$$
The input $K$ has finite Tor amplitude; no projection inverse outside this domain is used.

source.place: Refinement compatibility and naturality of the actual projection transformations

proof.text:
Let $\sigma$ denote the derived symmetry and $\lambda$ the left unitor. The symmetric monoidal structure of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor], specialized to the constant-$A$ ringed pro-etale site, gives
$$\sigma_{M,\omega_{c'}}(1_M\otimes b_A)=(b_A\otimes1_M)\sigma_{M,\omega_c}.$$
Define the actual transpose input from [def-pur-co-smoothness] by
$$a_c=\lambda_K(\varepsilon_{c,A}\otimes1_K)P_c(\omega_c,K)^{-1}F_c(\sigma_{M,\omega_c}).$$
Using the symmetry equation and naturality of $\rho$, followed by step 3, yields
$$a_{c'}F_{c'}(1_M\otimes b_A)\rho_{H_c}=\lambda_K((\varepsilon_{c',A}q)\otimes1_K)P_c(\omega_c,K)^{-1}F_c(\sigma_{M,\omega_c})=a_c.$$
The last equality is step 2; combining tensor factors uses the bifunctor law [lem-weil-derived-tensor-functorial]. This explicitly compares the whole projection-and-counit composite.

source.place: Expand and compare the canonical derived tensor transpose inputs

proof.text:
Apply $\Phi_{c'}^{H_c,K}$ to step 4 after cancelling $\rho_{H_c}$. Its source naturality and compactification compatibility [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] give, respectively,
$$\Phi_{c'}(a_{c'}F_{c'}(1_M\otimes b_A))=\theta^{c'}_K(1_M\otimes b_A),\qquad \Phi_{c'}(a_c\rho_{H_c}^{-1})=b_K\theta^c_K.$$
Equality of their arguments therefore proves exactly the asserted square. For a fixed compactification the transformations $P_c,\sigma,\lambda$ are maps in the pro-etale derived categories, not choices of etale representatives. Witness independence of $\Phi_c$ in the same cited theorem consequently makes $\Phi_c(a_c)$ unchanged when either witness is replaced, under the canonical identification of its source.

source.place: Transpose the explicit equality; independence of the etale-origin witnesses

proof.text: For three compactifications, [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] gives $b_{13}=b_{23}b_{12}$ and identity comparisons for identical choices. The bifunctor law [lem-weil-derived-tensor-functorial] gives $1_M\otimes b_{13,A}=(1_M\otimes b_{23,A})(1_M\otimes b_{12,A})$, including the identity case. Pasting the squares from step 5 proves the requested identity and cocycle laws for the identified maps. Witness changes leave the same derived map fixed, so obey the same laws. Finally take $c'$ to be the fixed compactification realizing the constructible functor in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Its defining transpose is $\theta_{f,K}$, so step 5 identifies every realization with that specified map.

source.place: Coherent choice independence and agreement with the specified tensor map
